description: Homescoope recipes pin upstream library versions in packages/*/recipe.yaml.
A custom regex manager reads `# renovate: …` comments above `version:` and opens one PR per package when upstream cuts a release.

Recipe automerge only for packages listed in scripts/ci-certified.json (full cert/*.mjs checklist + negative proof); the merge queue requires ci, which needs both reviewers' approval, and every publish is the reviewed PR artifact. Majors and new packages stay manual.

Extends the shared SLICC preset, which turns automerge on globally. Here, any merged change under packages/** can publish, so the rules below turn automerge off for packages/** majors and the publish-path workflows, and turn off @ai-ecoverse re-pins in shipped manifests entirely (they ride each package's next -N).

binutils.description: GNU binutils release tarballs (git tags are binutils-2_47, which no versioning reads as 2.47)

curl.description: curl release tarballs (tags are curl-8_22_0, which extractVersion can't turn into a version)

curl-cacert.description: curl's dated extracts of Mozilla's CA certificate store (cacert-YYYY-MM-DD.pem), for tls-engine's roots.der. A bump also needs the sha256 in packages/tls-engine/recipe.yaml and slicc.tls.roots in its package.json; the build fails closed until both match.

customManagers.description: Homebrew-shaped recipe.yaml upstream pins (see # renovate comments). depName is optional: a pin without one (perl-version, python-version, golang-version) is named after its datasource.
wasi-sdk pin in scripts/install-wasi-sdk.sh (# renovate comment above WASI_SDK_MAJOR). A bump also needs the two sha256 pins in that file; the install fails closed until they are updated.

packageRules.description: Anything under packages/** can publish once merged, so it may only merge through the merge queue, which requires ci on the PR head (every build job and both reviewers' approval), and every publish is that PR's reviewed artifact (#1085). So recipe bumps automerge like everything else (platformAutomerge); majors stay human (rules below).
Recipe bumps automerge (non-major): the queue's required ci includes the dual review, and an unapproved head can't merge.

Semver majors on recipes don't automerge: the homescoop coordinator's lane owns them. A worker checks the breaking changes, then merges on green ci (which includes the dual review). The weekly sweep picks up any major left waiting.
CI-certified packages (see scripts/ci-certified.json) — non-major only; automerge scope, not a publish gate. Synced by scripts/sync-ci-certified-renovate.mjs.

@ai-ecoverse dependencies in a shipped manifest (packages/*/package/package.json) are never updated by Renovate. Until #1698 the root workspaces made them internal workspace packages, which Renovate skips. A re-pin changes a shipped manifest without a new packaging revision, so npm-parity fails it (the package is on npm with different contents: #1702, #1703, #1707, #1708, #1709). Re-pins ride each package's next -N, made by its builder. This also covers every >=X.Y.Z-N <X.Y.Z+1 range, which Renovate's npm versioning rewrites wrongly. scripts/test/renovate-ranges.test.mjs checks it.

Shipped manifests (packages/*/package/package.json) keep the ranges of their other dependencies, such as wasm-emscripten's acorn ^8.18.0 (disabled today, rule below): consumers resolve within them, and the shared preset's pin would turn every bump into a -N release (#1700). replace leaves a range alone while the new version is inside it and bumps an exact pin to the new version. scripts/test/renovate-ranges.test.mjs checks it.
libpng 1.7 is a parallel beta line; stay on the 1.6.x stable series.
vim tags move fast; xxd tracks a pinned patch — ignore majors.

Workflow action pins get their own branches (renovate/actions-…). Renovate names a branch after the sanitized dependency name, so the action ai-ecoverse/slicc-shared-web and the npm devDependency @ai-ecoverse/slicc-shared-web both landed on renovate/ai-ecoverse-slicc-shared-web-1.x, one PR (#1270). A branch automerges only if every update in it does, so the ladder-build.yml action bump (manual, publish path) kept the root devDependency bump from automerging. scripts/test/renovate-branches.test.mjs checks no two managers share a branch.
Workflow action pins below a major.
The publish path (ladder-build.yml, the one workflow, including its slicc-shared-web pipeline pin): action and pin bumps there are reviewed by hand, never automerged.

The memory-peak step action in ladder-build.yml (ai-ecoverse/slicc-shared-web/.github/actions/memory-peak) automerges its minors and patches: every step is if: always() + continue-on-error: true and only prints the memory peak, so it can't change a build or a publish (#1715, #1734, #1742, #1745, #1753 were armed by hand). Renovate names it after the repo, like the pipeline.yml pin; depType action (a step) vs workflow (the reusable pipeline) tells them apart, so the pipeline pin and every other action there stay manual, and a slicc-shared-web branch that also moves the pipeline pin stays manual. scripts/test/renovate-ranges.test.mjs checks it.
github-script major bumps can break the workflow; review by hand.

py-* C++ side modules (numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, contourpy, kiwisolver): upstream bumps need a wasix side-module rebuild on the current sysroot runtimes and move the whole numpy C-API stack together; they ride homescoop#211 (py-* C++ stack v2), not single-package Renovate PRs (#31, #32, #38). Re-pins onto a new wasix-python are packaging-only repacks.

wasm-emscripten's third-party npm dependencies (typescript, esbuild-wasm, acorn, …) mirror upstream emscripten's own package.json at the pinned emscripten release, so they move with the emscripten version, never alone (#325: typescript 7 broke host-build). @ai-ecoverse pins are bumped by the builder.

Semver majors of anything (recipes, workflow actions, npm, Cargo) don't automerge: the homescoop coordinator's lane reviews the breaking changes and merges on green plus certified, and the weekly sweep keeps them owned.
crates/** (the shared Rust crates): a crates-only PR runs the crates checks but builds no dependent package, so CI would not test what a bump affects. Never automerge.

Root package.json devDependencies are our own test pins (cert kernel, shared harness, playwright). They automerge like the rest (Lars, 10-19): the queue requires ci (with the dual review) on the bump, and the kernel and shared-web are certified at latest. Majors stay human; slicc-kernel-negative stays disabled (rule below).
slicc-kernel-negative is the pinned old kernel (npm alias) the negative proofs must fail on (#393); a bump would break the proof.
Renovate has no perl-version datasource: wasix-perl's pin reads Perl's release tags (stable 5.even.N) instead, without touching the recipe.

Retired recipes (builder: retired): no Renovate PRs for any file in their package directory (recipe pins, Cargo.toml, go.mod). They are built, if at all, by their own workflows from pinned sources (e.g. wasi-rustc-stable.yml), so a recipe bump builds nothing. Synced by scripts/sync-ci-certified-renovate.mjs.
